summary.intent: Run the GSD discuss-phase, plan-phase, and ui-phase workflows for Phase 21 (BYO-IPFS Node Support) to capture implementation decisions, conduct technical research, and generate a UI design contract.
summary.outcome: CONTEXT.md was created with locked decisions (three-mode pinning, client-direct architecture, TEE-based migration, zero-knowledge auth), RESEARCH.md and VALIDATION.md were generated, and the ui-phase workflow was initiated to produce a UI-SPEC.md.

repo: The original PROJECT.md planned a server-relay approach for BYO-IPFS v1.1 with client-direct deferred to v1.2, but the discussion revised this to client-direct in v1.1 since the SDK already exists.
BYO-IPFS auth token storage was an open concern in STATE.md — resolved to zero-knowledge: credentials stored in vault metadata on IPFS, encrypted with user key, decrypted client-side only.
The TEE (Phala Cloud) is already used for IPNS republishing background jobs, making it a natural fit for pin migration — encrypted blobs can be moved without the TEE ever seeing plaintext content.
The existing IpfsService has a provider interface (ipfs-provider.interface.ts) with a local provider implementation — BYO-IPFS adds a RemotePinningProvider at the SDK layer.
Quota tracking is advisory (no enforcement) for BYO-IPFS — CipherBox API only registers CIDs for bookkeeping, not to gate uploads.
PSA (Pinning Service API) and Kubo RPC both need to be supported with auto-detection during connection test due to different provider offerings.

workflow: The GSD auto-advance chain (discuss → plan → execute) was not used here; each phase was invoked manually.
The ui-phase gate in plan-phase requires a UI-SPEC.md before planning for frontend phases — user must run /gsd:ui-phase first when this gate triggers.
ROADMAP.md success criteria (SC#2, BYO-02) will need manual updating to reflect scope changes made during discussion — the workflow doesn't automatically update the roadmap.
The discuss-phase workflow correctly identified a scope change mid-discussion (server-relay → client-direct) and surfaced it before locking decisions.

friction: The plan-phase workflow stopped at the UI design contract gate and required a separate /gsd:ui-phase invocation, breaking the flow — user had to start over with a new command.
Original PROJECT.md architectural decisions (server-relay for v1.1) were stale and conflicted with the emerging design — required explicit acknowledgment during discussion to override.
open_items: ROADMAP.md success criteria SC#2 and BYO-02 need updating to reflect three-mode pinning model and client-direct architecture instead of server-relay dual-pin.
